source_text:
Ὕδρωψ, ἔστιν ἔκκλισις ἄλογος ψυχῆς, καθ' ἣν σβεσθεισῶν τῶν ἀρετῶν
ἐπικρατεῖ κακία καὶ ἀγνωσία. ΙΖʹ. Μύρμηξ, ἔστιν ἄνθρωπος πρακτικὸς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ τροφὴν ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τούτῳ παρασκευάζων. ΙΗʹ. Χοιρογρύλλιοι, εἰσὶν ἔθνη ἀκάθαρτα τὰς ἐντολὰς δεξάμενα τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Χριστοῦ. ΙΘʹ. Ἀβασίλευτοι ἀκρίδες, ψυχαὶ λογικαὶ μὴ σαλευόμεναι ὑπὸ τοῦ θανάτου καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν σπερμάτων διατρεφόμεναι. Κʹ. Ἀσκαλαβότης, ἔστι νοῦς πρακτικὸς, ἐπερειδόμενος ἀρεταῖς καὶ κατοικῶν ἐν ταῖς γνώσεσι τῶν οὐρανίων δυνάμεων. ΚΑʹ. Σκύμνος λέοντος, ἔστιν ἄνθρωπος ἀπαθὴς τῶν ἐν αὐτῷ γενομένων βασιλεύσας θηρίων. 40.1268 ΚΒʹ. Ἀλεκτρυὼν, ἔστιν ἄνθρωπος πνευματικὸς πληρούμενος γνώσεως καὶ ἑτέραις εὐαγγελιζόμενος ψυχαῖς τὴν παρὰ τοῦ νοητοῦ ἡλίου γενομένην ἡμέραν. ΚΓʹ. Τράγος, ἔστιν ἀνὴρ πρακτικὸς τῶν ἐν αὐτῷ ἀτάκτων λογισμῶν ὀρθῶς καθηγούμενος. 1 Κ∆ʹ.
thought_title: Dropsy and the symbolic animals of spiritual progress
orientation: Evagrius continues his list of spiritual diseases and then begins a series of symbolic animals and natural figures representing practitioners at different stages of spiritual progress.
pass_a_gloss: Dropsy is an irrational turning away of the soul, according to which, when the virtues have been quenched, vice and ignorance prevail. 17. An ant is a practical man preparing his own food in this age. 18. Rock badgers are unclean nations that received the commandments of our Savior Christ. 19. Unruled locusts are rational souls not shaken by death and nourished by seeds. 20. A gecko is a practical mind, leaning on virtues and dwelling in the knowledges of the heavenly powers. 21. A lion cub is a man free from passions who has ruled over the beasts that came to be in him. 22. A rooster is a spiritual man filled with knowledge and announcing to other souls the day that has come to be from the intelligible sun. 23. A he-goat is a practical man rightly leading the disorderly thoughts in him.

choices.why: Keeps the noun force of ἔκκλισις as a movement of the soul, with ἄλογος as its quality; literal and diagnostic.

choices.english: when the virtues have been quenched
choices.why: The genitive absolute is causal-circumstantial; 'quenched' preserves the fire imagery of σβέννυμι.
rejected: after the virtues are put out

choices.why: ἐπικρατεῖ is singular with two subjects; 'prevail' keeps the verb's force of gaining mastery.
πρακτικός is the technical term for the ascetic practitioner; 'practical man' is literal and consistent with the brief's practical virtues.
ἀβασίλευτος means 'without a king'; 'unruled' is literal and keeps the political metaphor.
ἐπερείδω means to rest or lean upon; the dative ἀρεταῖς is instrumental, and 'leaning on' keeps the physical image.

pass_b_english: Dropsy is an irrational turning away of the soul, in which vice and ignorance prevail once the virtues have been quenched.
An ant is a practical man who prepares his own food in this age.
Rock badgers are unclean nations that have received the commandments of our Savior Christ.
Unruled locusts are rational souls that are not shaken by death and are fed by seeds.
A gecko is a practical mind that leans on virtues and dwells in the knowledge of the heavenly powers.
A lion cub is a man free from passions who has ruled the beasts within him.
A rooster is a spiritual man who is filled with knowledge and proclaims to other souls the day that has come from the intelligible sun.
A he-goat is a practical man who rightly leads the disordered thoughts within him.

last_rejected.quote: A rooster is a spiritual man who is filled with knowledge and proclaims to other souls the day that has come from the intelligible sun.
last_rejected.source_quote: Ἀλεκτρυὼν, ἔστιν ἄνθρωπος πνευματικὸς πληρούμενος γνώσεως καὶ ἑτέραις εὐαγγελιζόμενος ψυχαῖς τὴν παρὰ τοῦ νοητοῦ ἡλίου γενομένην ἡμέραν.
last_rejected.why: Missing 'evangelizing/proclaiming good news' force of εὐαγγελιζόμενος; 'proclaims' loses gospel nuance.
last_rejected.fix: and evangelizes to other souls the day that has come from the intelligible sun.
last_rejected.ruling: εὐαγγελιζόμενος rendered as 'proclaims' conveys announcement; gospel nuance is minor, overall meaning retained.

problems.quote: A gecko is a practical mind that leans on virtues
problems.why: 'Practical man' and 'practical mind' seem to describe same stage but different subjects; reader may think these are different categories.
problems.fix: Clarify 'practical' modifies type of life, not person vs faculty

problems.quote: A rooster is a spiritual man who is filled with knowledge
problems.why: Three 'man' types with different modifiers; unclear if hierarchical progression or parallel categories.
problems.fix: Indicate these are ascending or distinct stages

problems.quote: A mocking eye is an unclean power
problems.why: Singular/plural and nominal/adjectival forms may obscure that same entity type intended.

problems.quote: A gecko is a practical mind that leans on virtues and dwells in the knowledge of the heavenly powers
problems.why: 'Leans on virtues' is vague; gecko's physical clinging not connected to spiritual meaning.
problems.fix: 'clings to virtues' to preserve animal metaphor

problems.quote: Unruled locusts are rational souls that are not shaken by death and are fed by seeds
problems.why: 'Fed by seeds' seems positive but locusts are biblical plague; 'seeds' may mean 'seed-plots' or 'seed-like words'?
problems.fix: Check if 'seeds' should be 'seed-words' or 'divine sowings'

problems.quote: Rock badgers are unclean nations that have received the commandments of our Savior Christ
problems.why: Leviticus 11:5 calls rock badger unclean, but no nation receives commandments in that text; Proverbs 30:26 praises their wisdom.
problems.fix: Note this is Evagrius's allegorical application, not direct citation

problems.why: Same concept rendered three ways; reader may think they differ.
problems.fix: Standardize or note they are equivalent.

problems.why: 'Work of virtue' and 'practical virtues' may be the same concept.
Both appear in same section for similar concepts; distinction unclear.
problems.fix: Clarify whether 'man' and 'mind' are interchangeable here.

problems.quote: Unruled locusts are rational souls that are not shaken by death
problems.why: 'Unruled' does not fit the positive description that follows.
problems.fix: Check Greek; possibly 'unwinged' or a specific locust type from Lev 11.

edits.old: A gecko is a practical mind that leans on virtues
edits.new: A gecko is a practical mind that clings to virtues

fixed: Glossary: 'practical man' vs 'practical mind' — the source uses ἄνθρωπος πρακτικός for ant, lion cub, he-goat and νοῦς πρακτικός for gecko; the distinction is in the source, not a translation error. No edit.
Glossary: 'spiritual man' vs 'practical man' — the source uses distinct terms (πνευματικός vs πρακτικός); the English preserves this. No edit.
Glossary: 'unclean power' — not present in this section. No edit.
Unreadable: 'leans on virtues' — the source has ἐπερειδόμενος ἀρεταῖς, 'leaning/supporting oneself on virtues'; 'clings to' better preserves the gecko's physical clinging. Edited.
Mistranslation: 'fed by seeds' — the source has ὑπὸ τῶν σπερμάτων διατρεφόμεναι, literally 'nourished by seeds'; the English is accurate. No edit.
Wrong scripture: rock badgers — the source does not cite scripture; the English does not either. No edit.
Glossary: 'rational soul' — the source uses ψυχαὶ λογικαί consistently; the English renders it consistently. No edit.
Glossary: 'practical virtues' — not present in this section. No edit.
Glossary: 'practical man' vs 'practical mind' — the source distinguishes ἄνθρωπος πρακτικός from νοῦς πρακτικός; the English preserves this. No edit.
Mistranslation: 'unruled locusts' — the source has ἀβασίλευτοι ἀκρίδες, 'kingless/unruled locusts'; the English is accurate. No edit.
